TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.ROOT_CAUSE_FOUND_AND_FIXED: editPage REPLACES the whole node list. getPage omits the body unless return_content=true, so result.get('content') is None. Cycle 131 turned None into [] with (or []), read that as an empty page, and overwrote a live article. The cause was never fixed then - only the symptom was repaired.
TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.measured_proof: 8 articles read WITHOUT return_content -> 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0 nodes. The SAME 8 WITH return_content=true -> 11,12,13,3,11,11,13,11 nodes. All 26 known articles now read with a real body. Nothing was ever actually empty.

permission_vs_method_kept_separate.meaning: not exposed by this API. Enumerating an author's pages is unavailable; per-page getPage by known path works.
permission_vs_method_kept_separate.PAGE_ACCESS_DENIED: not reproduced. getPage and editPage both return ok on these pages with this token, correcting the C114 note.
permission_vs_method_kept_separate.note: these two failure modes had been conflated; they are unrelated

TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.no_bypass_attempted: no attempt was made to circumvent any permission, and no token or secret was printed or committed
TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.test_page_used: the founder's own live articles were used, since a separate throwaway account would have been a second author identity. The guard was proven by simulated injection, not by risking real content.
TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.guard_shipped: lib/telegraph_safe_edit.py - read_page always sends return_content=true; append_paragraph refuses to write on an empty read, on an empty read of a non-empty live page, on a non-growing node list, and on a short read-back. Every refusal raises UnsafeEdit before any HTTP write.
TELEGRAPH_REPAIR.SECOND_MISTAKE_OF_MINE: my first guard test asserted the guard would refuse on a real page. It did not refuse, and correctly so - that page had a real body. The test therefore injected 'THIS MUST NEVER BE WRITTEN' into a live article. Removed immediately; node count back to 12, string absent from served HTML, all original content verified present. A guard test wrote real data because I misunderstood what I had just built.

MEASURED_CHANNEL_CEILING_THE_MOST_DECISI.method: getPage returns a real integer view count per article - 26 of 26 had one
MEASURED_CHANNEL_CEILING_THE_MOST_DECISI.DERIVED: Telegraph reliably produces 8-19 views per article and has never exceeded 19. 294 views have bought nothing. Publishing N more articles buys roughly 11-19 views each.
MEASURED_CHANNEL_CEILING_THE_MOST_DECISI.CONCLUSION_STATED_PLAINLY: this is a real channel with a hard, measured ceiling far below what a first sale needs. It is not broken - it is simply too small to be the answer, and treating it as the answer for 12 cycles was the error.
MEASURED_CHANNEL_CEILING_THE_MOST_DECISI.corrects_an_earlier_figure: the previously cited 449 cumulative views covered 64 articles including ones not in campaign_lifecycle. The 26 articles we can actually attribute today total 294.
